newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions -Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions -Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA, Nov 18 - Montreal - All terminals working normally, no delays. 19 Nov - Vancouver - GRAIN - 6 Vessels loading, 11 waiting, delays 7-10 days depending on grade. 12 Due to load 20-29/11. COAL - Roberts Bank - 2 Loading, 3 waiting, delays 1-2 days, 6 due before 30/11, 24 due in Dec. Prince Rupert - 1 Loading, 4 waiting, delays to 10 days depending on grade to be loaded.

HONDURAS, Nov 18 - Puerto Cortes - Eight vessels berthed of which 3 discharging/loading containers, 2 loading bananas, 1 discharging coal, 1 wheat, 1 fertiliser. 4 Awaiting berths of which 3 to discharge/load containers, 1 to load bananas/ discharge containers. 13 Due, 5 to discharge/load containers, 4 to discharge/load general cargo, 4 to load bananas. Weather extremely bad. Nov 19 - Four vessels berthed, 2 loading bananas, 1 discharging coal, 1 wheat. 2 Waiting to discharge fertiliser. 13 Due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 4 to load bananas, 1 to discharge fuel oil. No berthing delays expected.

MEXICO, Nov 19 - All ports working normally. Tampico - Twelve vessels in port of which 3 containers, 1 pipes, 1 iron, 1 steel plates, 1 gar, 1 general cargo, 1 zinc, 1 cement, 1 corn, 1 gas. 1 Coal/general cargo vessel anchored. Altamira - Two vessels in port of which 1 fertiliser, 1 under repair. Vera Cruz - Nine vessels in port of which 1 pipes, 1 sugar, 3 corn, 2 grain, 1 coal, 1 under repair. Manzanillo - Ten vessels in port of which 2 general cargo, 2 cars, 3 containers, 1 sulphur, 2 grain. Coatzacoalcos - Seventeen vessels in port of which 9 chemicals, 7 oil tankers, 1 vessel under repair.

PANAMA, Nov 18 - Balboa - One bulker, 1 tanker. Cristobal - One container carrier, 1 general cargo, 1 vehicle carrier. Panama Canal - Waterway at full capacity, many panamax arrivals. Booking system allocation back to normal. 31 Vessels due, 20 in queue, 11 booked, 37 scheduled. Nov 17 Actual arrivals 27, transits 37. Average of booked and non-booked canal waters time, 27.6 hours

UNITED STATES, Nov 18 - Jersey City, NJ, Perth Amboy, NJ, Bayway, NJ - No vessels. Port Newark, NJ - Three vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ - Two vessels in port. Cartaret, NJ - Two vessels in port. All northern New Jersey ports working normally, no congestion/delay. Baltimore, MD - Port working normally. Eight bulkers, 3 container vessels, 2 ro/ros, 3 auto vessels, 2 tankers, 3 general cargo vessels. 1 Cable vessel on standby, 3 vessels in repair yard, 1 bulker awaiting berth and under arrest. Hampton Roads, VA - Four general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating, 2 vessels berthed loading coal, 3 anchored waiting to load, 1 bulker discharging cement, 1 alumina, 1 loading fertiliser. 1 Tanker discharging crude oil, 4 vessels berthed under repair.

East Coast - Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal this week. Elevators and coal operations working normally, no delays. Average waiting time at Consol coal 4 days. Liquid bulk facilities working normally. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis. Charleston, SC - Berth congestion continues at North Charleston terminal. 7 Oil tankers due this week. High winds and approaching front from N/NW threatens production levels at container terminals as well as vessel ETAs. Jacksonville, FL - No heavy berthing congestion at Jacksonville or Fernandina Beach. Miami, FL - No congestion at container berths. Gantry and ro/ro berths available all week. Passenger terminals available Tuesday-Thursday and from Friday 0600 hrs to Monday 1900 hrs passenger terminals will be in full operation.

New York, NY - No congestion at New York anchorages, none at container, tanker or sugar terminals. Norfolk, VA - Southern co pier - 15 Vessels due this week. At present, 2 vessels anchored waiting to load. Dominion terminal - 6 Vessels due. Pier ix coal terminal - 5 Vessels due this week. Cargill - 1 Vessel due this week. Container and general cargo terminals - working normally, no delays. Oil and bulk terminals - also working normally. All channels open with prevailing depths available. Philadelphia, PA - No congestion at Philadelphia, Camden or Wilmington. No dredging/repairs/navigational problems. Savannah, GA - No congestion for either Garden City terminals (container port) or Ocean terminals (break bulk) for next week. Colonial Marine terminals (bulk clay) expect a 1-2 day wait for all vessels. All liquid bulk facilities working normally, no congestion expected. Navigational conditions normal.

Gulf Coast, Houston, TX - No congestion at city docks, Houston and Galveston grain elevators. Congestion does exist, however, at some oil/chemical terminals. Mobile, AL - No congestion. Maintenance dredging of main channel continues. New Orleans, LA - Normal summer rains causing delay to cargo operations, especially grain loading. River stage at 6 feet, expected to rise to 8 feet by 22/11. Normal transit times expected. Bar pilots advise that Saturday and Sunday drafts for Mississippi Gulf outlet will be 30 feet. Present max Permissible draft at Southwest Pass is 47 feet fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt, 46 feet fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Some elevators not working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments.

West Coast, Columbia River - Grain vessel activity on the increase. Oregon/Washington ports entering rainy season which will slow grain elevator production. Coos Bay, OR - Slow for the past few weeks. No traffic at the beginning of the week. A lumber vessel and woodchip vessel arrived during the latter part of last week. Another woodchip carrier due over the weekend. The remainder of November appears to be slow.

Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan (lb-212-214) looks moderate for November. At present, 1-2 days berthing delay expected. Koch Carbon (lb-211) - 1 Vessel due for November at present. Kaiser (la-49) - Appears moderate for November (coal/petcoke). Delays of 1-2 days expected. November looks moderate for bulk cargoes, but December expected busier. San Francisco, CA - Oil spill cleanup largely completed but still some areas under the existing piers where oil remains. Fog also becoming a factor in movements of vessels, especially those in the river.
